title: Piper PA-28-161 Warrior II — Normal Operating Procedures (independently worded)
description: Normal procedure checklist for the Piper PA-28-161 Warrior II, a low-wing fixed-gear trainer with a Lycoming O-320 engine, fixed-pitch propeller, and manual flap lever. Fuel selector (LEFT / RIGHT / BOTH) is a key operational difference from high-wing trainers — confirm the detent is engaged at each selection. Wing fuel levels can be checked visually through small windows in the leading edge. No airspeeds, power settings, fuel quantities, or other numerical limits are stated — those must come from the specific aircraft's POH. Verify every item against the actual aircraft before flight.

source.notes: No manufacturer document was consulted or copied. This file was authored from general familiarity with the PA-28-161 type. Numerical limitations — airspeeds, power settings, fuel quantities, temperatures, pressures — are deliberately absent and must be supplied from the aircraft's own POH.

known_issues.description: Contains no airspeeds, power settings, fuel quantities or other limitations — must come from aircraft POH.
Equipment variations exist across this model/variant. Verify items against the specific aircraft before use.

rights.notes: Manufacturer POH remains under copyright. This file does not reproduce its wording or selection of items.

items.text: Carburetor heat — apply FULL HOT; note RPM response; return to COLD

items.detail: A rough engine followed by recovery during the carb heat check indicates ice was present. The Lycoming O-320 is susceptible to carb ice across a wide temperature range in moist air. Return heat to COLD before applying takeoff power.
